conventions.convention: A unitary fusion category has a positive C*-dagger structure, orthogonal semisimple decompositions, dagger-compatible tensor product, and unitary associators and unitors. A unitary braiding is additional structure.
V_ab^c is Hom(a⊗b,c), with f g† = ⟨f,g⟩ id_c; the inner product is linear in the first variable.
R_ab^c represents inverse-precomposition f ↦ f ∘ c_ab^−1, mapping V_ab^c to V_ba^c. It records inverse object-braiding eigenvalues.
F represents f ↦ f ∘ α^−1 from left-tree to right-tree Hom coordinates; rows index target channels and multiplicities, columns source channels and multiplicities.
New basis columns equal old basis columns multiplied by G. Consequently F′ = G_R^−1 F G_L and R′ = (G_ba^c)^−1 R G_ab^c.
External and internal fusion-tree charges are fixed simple-object representatives, with every vertex multiplicity retained. Zero-dimensional coordinate spaces use unique empty matrices.
Fibonacci pullback phases are x = exp(−4πi/5), y = exp(3πi/5), with object-braiding phases x^−1 and y^−1. The nontrivial F block uses channel order (1,τ).

The Ising example supplies only the three-σ, total-σ sector: channel order (1,ψ), Hadamard F, and pullback phases exp(−πi/8), exp(3πi/8). It asserts no complete Ising category or global ribbon coherence.
Modularity means that transparent simples consist only of the tensor unit; transparent objects include the zero object and all finite sums of the unit.
Framed-link invariance assumes countable choice, common color, and positive strand counts. Ordinary Markov stabilization changes framing; modularity is unnecessary.
The Hecke counterexamples use the root normalization (T_i−v)(T_i+1)=0 at v=2.

load_bearing.statement: A unitary fusion category is a complex fusion category equipped with the specified positive C*-dagger structure, orthogonal semisimple decompositions, dagger-compatible tensor product, and unitary associator and unit constraints.

For simple representative inputs and total charge in a unitary fusion category, the fusion-tree vectors form an orthonormal basis of Hom(T,d). Their number is the sum over admissible charge labelings of products of vertex fusion multiplicities; the left-associated recursion is m_n(d)=Σ_e m_(n−1)(e)N_(e a_n)^d for n≥2, with the stated empty and one-input values.

Let a,b,c be simple objects in a unitary fusion category. The pairing on V_ab^c=Hom(a⊗b,c) defined by f g†=⟨f,g⟩id_c is a finite-dimensional positive-definite Hermitian inner product, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second.
F_d^abc is defined by L_(e,μ,ν) ∘ α_abc^−1 = Σ_(f,ρ,σ) F_d^abc[(f,ρ,σ),(e,μ,ν)] R_(f,ρ,σ), retaining every charge and multiplicity index.
For simple a,b,c in a unitary braided fusion category, the channel exchange is the pullback R_ab^c(f)=f ∘ c_ab^−1 from V_ab^c to V_ba^c; its matrix in orthonormal multiplicity bases is the R-symbol.

The specified skeletal finite-direct-sum category, fusion rules, strict unit gauge, F blocks and pullback R phases define a Fibonacci unitary braided fusion category; the verification checks all simple-input pentagon and hexagon sectors and rigidity.

For a crossing word acting by f ↦ f ∘ b_β^−1, a unitary multiplicity-basis change gives U_β′=G_L′^−1 U_β G_L. For n≥2 identical simple strand charges, adjacent exchanges define a unitary B_n representation on the fixed-total fusion space, including the zero-dimensional case.

Scalar endomorphisms of complex simple charges and nonzero identities; existence and uniqueness of scalar Hom pairings.
Linear-first Hermitian convention, positive definiteness, and scalar norm calculation in both counterexamples.
Unitarity requires an invertible norm-preserving map; scalar multiplication by 2 cannot qualify.
Balancing, unit twist, and dual compatibility in the local ribbon definition.
Typed braiding isomorphisms, naturality, and both exact hexagon identities.
Associator direction, bifunctoriality, pentagon, triangle, and unit constraints.

Invertibility and the cubic equation, interpreted in a strict model, for the scalar counterexample.
An algebraic Yang–Baxter operator supplies braid representations without supplying a positive inner product.
Adjacent braid relations, distant commutation, and the B3 matrix checks.
The exact root normalization and valid specialization v↦2 in both counterexamples.
Extension of generator assignments satisfying the Artin relators.
Equality of canonical rebracketings when local Artin composites are inserted into longer trees.
The explicit ACω hypothesis carried by framed-link evaluation.
The precise root trace t_n and its distinction from the choice-dependent tangle-functor comparison.
Equality for framed-isotopic, common-color blackboard closures under ACω; stabilization changes framing.
The counterexample's remark correctly limits compact-group averaging to continuous representations of compact Hausdorff groups.
The counterexample's remark that B3 maps onto the integers and is infinite.

concerns.concern: The empty-input assertion says “m_0(d)=1 if d=1 and 0 otherwise,” and step 1.1 argues that an isomorphism 1→d exists “exactly when d=1.” However, def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis only fixes a set of simple representatives; it never requires that the actual tensor-unit object belong to that set. An allowed representative d≅1 with d≠1 has dim Hom(1,d)=1, whereas the stated formula gives zero and the definition supplies no empty-tree vector. The missing convention that the unit represents its own class must be resolved in the defining interface.

Step 1.2 fixes total charge d, constructs inclusions of d into T, and then says “Their projections sum to id_T.” For a fixed d they sum to the d-isotypic projection, generally not id_T; for example, T=τ⊗τ=1⊕τ and d=1. Summing over all simple outputs gives id_T, and the fixed-d part gives completeness of Hom(T,d). This is a short repair to the proof, independent of the empty-input issue.

The Nayak source locator says “§IV.B.c ... Fibonacci fusion rule, F-matrix, R phases, and basis conventions.” In the [source](https://arxiv.org/html/0707.1889v2), the fusion rule is in the opening of IV.B, F and tree bases are in (a), Eqs. (161)–(164), and R phases are in (b), Eqs. (167)–(170). Subsection (c) begins “Computing with Fibonacci Anyons.” The local mathematical verification is present, but the subsection locator is inaccurate.

alerts.finding: thm-qc-tqc-braid-action-unitary-and-artin, step 2.1, says “restriction to V(x^n→c) preserves the same relations” and “these restricted operators are exactly T_i^−1 R_i T_i.” Its cited canonical-action supplier acts on the object x^⊗n by local c, whereas V=Hom(x^⊗n,c) is a multiplicity Hom space and the assigned R definition uses inverse-precomposition by c. Restriction to an object-level isotypic block does not literally produce this Hom action. The proof needs the short passage b↦(f↦f∘b^−1), including its composition law; thm-qc-tqc-gauge-covariance supplies that argument explicitly.

ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-qubit-matrices cites Nayak with locator “§IV.B.c, PDF pp. 53–57.” Its displayed F and braid matrices occur in IV.B(a)–(b), specifically Eqs. (164), (169), and (170), before (c) starts. This is directly checkable in https://arxiv.org/html/0707.1889v2 around the IV.2 Fibonacci section. The quoted data agree with the assigned supplier; the subsection locator needs correction.

The Fibonacci pivotal construction uses the supplied coherent category and inverse object-braiding phases; the full Ising construction supplies its own all-label coherence rather than importing it from the sector example.

The page and consumers retain the fixed Fibonacci chirality, channel order, fusion dimensions, and Ising sector limitation. The all-m Majorana identification is explicitly an interface hypothesis.
